title: Video review coaching and operative skill in general surgery residents
subtitle: Design not yet settled; programme size, procedures, rating method, time and approvals not stated
statement: Some general surgery residents review videos of their laparoscopic operations with a consultant, and the programme believes this helps, but nobody has measured whether coached residents gain operative skill faster than residents who are not coached. The request does not state how many residents there are, which operations are filmed, how skill would be judged, or what time and approvals are available; these need to be settled before a design can be chosen.
whoAffected: General surgery residents, the consultants who coach them, programme leadership, and patients whose operations are performed by trainees under supervision.
whatHurts: If coaching works, residents who are not coached progress more slowly; if it does not, consultant time is spent without benefit. Filming also raises questions of consent and of how videos might be used in assessment.
currentPractice: Video review happens informally for some residents with some consultants; there is no schedule, no skill measure and no list of who is coached.
whyNow: Filming equipment is already in the theatres and residents are using it, so the question can be answered at little cost if it is framed before the next academic year.
patientCenteredGoal: Patients operated on by trainees receive operations performed with the skill that effective coaching would bring, earlier in training.
summary: Problem framed from a brief request; the design family is left unresolved and the missing details are listed for the investigator.
